| `content`    | `object`             |          | `\{\}`  | The list config: `{ register, schema, filter?, sort?, limit?, offset?, extend?, presentation?, variant?, lead?, leading?, title?, meta?, text?, label?, pill?, trailing?, icon?, aggregates?, rowRoute?, rowIdField?, headerLink?, headerNote?, emptyText?, errorText?, valueLabels?, endpointSource?, bar? }`. `bar` (`{ valueField, maxField?, overVariant? }`) draws a thin track under each row: filled to `valueField` against `maxField` (drawn in the error colour past it with `overVariant: "error"`), or without `maxField` against the largest row. `endpointSource` (`{ url, method?, params?, responsePath? }`) reads the rows from an app endpoint instead of `register` / `schema`. `objectRows` (`{ path, where?, valuePath? }`) lists rows the page record holds, with no request. `valueLabels` maps a field's stored values to the labels the templates show. `headerNote` and `headerLink.label` fill `{total}` and `{count:&lt;field&gt;=&lt;value&gt;}`, the loaded rows with that value. A row that is a plain string or number (an endpoint answering `["…", "…"]`) is read as `{ value }`: templates reach it as `{value}`, and without `title` a row shows the value itself. `presentation: "notice"` draws the rows as sentences in one box toned by `variant` (`info`, `warning` or `error`), after an optional `lead` (`{total}` filled in). `dot` (a field, or `{ field, colorMap? }`) draws a colour dot before the title; `flags` (`[{ field, label, value? }]`) draws the labels of the flags a row has ("Start", "End") at its end. `tiles: true` (rows only) draws each row as a framed tile in a grid of 260px at the least. `footerLink` (the shape of `headerLink`) ends the card with a text link under the rows. `footerAction` (`{ label, icon?, type, ..., disabledWhen?, disabledReason? }`) ends the card with one action, also under the empty text; while the visibleWhen condition `disabledWhen` holds the button is disabled and `disabledReason` shows under it. `note` is a line above it and `wide: true` stretches it across the card. A list of such actions draws the first whose `visibleWhen` (a local condition over the page's record) holds (DqZaaktype Versies: "Publiceren" on a draft, "Nieuwe versie maken" otherwise). `pill.cases` (`[{ when, label, variant? }]`) labels a row by the first case whose `when` holds on it, else by the pill's own `label` and `variant` (Concept, Vastgezet, Actief). `footnoteVariant` (`info`, `warning` or `error`) draws the footnote as a toned notice box with its icon (DqZaaktype opt-out note). `tableLook: "data"` marks a `table` as a data table, which the board look draws as its card table (header band, 40px rows, hairlines) instead of the compact grid (DqZaaktype "Berichten aan de aanvrager"). `groupBy` (a field path) draws the rows in groups under a heading per value, headed by the field's `valueLabels` entry; `groupOrder` (values) orders the groups and `groupEmptyLabel` heads the rows without a value. `density: "compact"` draws the rows 10px above and below, at least 56px tall, with the title at 500 (DqProcesanalyse). In `rows`, `text` is a line under the meta line ("12 dagen stil"), and `chevron: false` leaves the chevron off a linked row (DqDashboard). `presentation: "checklist"` draws the rows in `columns` (default 3), a row for which `done` (a condition over the row) holds ticked, and `progress: true` adds a bar of the done share (DqTenant Inrichten); `headerNote` can say "\{count:status=completed\} of \{total\} steps done". `aggregates` (`{ key: { register, schema, op: "count" \| "max", field?, where, text? } }`, `@self.&lt;path&gt;` in `where` read off the row) asks a figure over each row's related objects, as a table's `aggregate` column does, and offers it to the row's templates as `{key}`; `text` (`{ zero?, one?, other }` with `{count}`) offers a count as words (DqZaaktype Versies "31 lopende zaken", "geen lopende zaken"). In `rows`, `ruleAbove: true` rules above the first row too, and `pillAt: "start"` draws the pill before the title (DqZaakDocumenten "Weigeringsgronden tot nu toe"). |
